amendments.body: The depth-weighted average porosity in `effective_substrate_porosity` (systems/substrate.rs:127-139) may significantly overestimate O₂ penetration when a low-porosity top layer (e.g., fine sand, porosity 0.35) sits above a high-porosity deep layer (e.g., lava rock, porosity 0.55). In reality, the top layer's porosity is the rate-limiting bottleneck for surface-to-depth O₂ diffusion. The weighted average dilutes this constraint with the deeper layer's porosity, producing a D_eff that's too high. Consider using the porosity of the topmost layer (or the layer at the penetration boundary) instead of the depth-weighted average across the full stack, or document this as a known limitation with a TODO for heterogeneous-stack correction.
amendments.rationale: The Bouldin model assumes homogeneous substrate. When applied to a heterogeneous stack with a depth-weighted average, the physical meaning breaks down: O₂ must diffuse *through* the top layer before reaching deeper layers, so the top layer porosity governs effective diffusivity. A 1cm sand cap (porosity 0.35) on 4cm lava rock (porosity 0.55) would compute D_eff using porosity ~0.51, overestimating penetration by ~(0.51/0.35)² ≈ 2.1×. This could lead to unrealistically deep oxic zones in capped substrates, which would underestimate denitrification potential (the downstream consumer in E4b).

amendments.body: Convenience accessors `substrate_oxic_volume_cm3()`, `substrate_oxic_pore_volume_cm3()`, `substrate_suboxic_volume_cm3()`, `substrate_suboxic_pore_volume_cm3()` in state.rs:266-279 each independently call `substrate_*_zone_geometry()`, which internally calls `substrate_o2_penetration_depth_cm()` (iterating all layers) and then iterates all layers again for geometry. Any tick-level code path that calls multiple of these accessors (or calls them alongside the full geometry accessors) redundantly recomputes the same values. Consider removing these single-field convenience accessors, or at minimum adding a doc comment warning callers to prefer `substrate_zone_geometry()` when they need more than one metric.
amendments.rationale: Each convenience accessor is O(2n) in the number of substrate layers (n for penetration depth, n for geometry accumulation). Callers needing both oxic and suboxic metrics (e.g., future denitrification in E4b, which needs suboxic volume, plus nitrogen cycling which may need oxic volume) would trigger 4 full traversals instead of 2. This is unlikely to be a bottleneck with typical 1-3 layers, but the API design invites inefficient usage patterns that could surprise downstream implementers.

payload.summary: Reviewed the substrate oxic/suboxic zone implementation across 10 changed files (~650 lines). The implementation is well-structured: the shared O₂ penetration boundary design, sentinel-based legacy detection, zone geometry accessors, and habitat mapping are all sound. All 74+ tests pass. The code correctly implements the Bouldin steady-state model, properly handles stacked layers with a single shared redox boundary, and round-trips through save/load including legacy save migration. Found two issues worth noting — one correctness gap in the porosity model and one performance concern.
